newsitem.title: USA: Report says prospects good for college graduates.
newsitem.headline: Report says prospects good for college graduates.

text.p: College graduates will find a fatter market for jobs into the new year, with the greatest opportunities in the north central and southeastern states, a survey said Monday.

Overall there will be a more than a 6 percent increase in job prospects, Michigan State University said in its 1996-97 survey of hiring prospects, "thus sustaining an expanding job market for new graduates over four consecutive years."
The school said it contacted 508 businesses, industries and governmental agencies for its annual report.
While there are opportunities in all geographic areas, the southeast and north central regions offered "the most favourable job prospects for new graduates," it said.

"Shortages of new graduates are reported for computer science majors, computer programmers, systems analysts, computer engineers, marketing and sales, actuaries, transportation and logistic management majors and electrical engineers," the report said.
Starting salaries are likely to be as much as 4 percent higher than a year ago, the repport said, with the highest starting salary -- $42,758 -- waiting for chemical engineers.
